source.title: Winning Ticket in Noisy Image Classiﬁcation
source.authors: Taehyeon Kim; Jongwoo Ko; J. Choi; Sangwook Cho; Seyoung Yun

record.tranche_reason: Reports test accuracy under several fractions of artificially corrupted image labels, but does not measure training error or test the other listed behaviors.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on fitting random labels; those cited results are not this study’s rows. Its own noisy-label experiments report test accuracy across noise conditions, but not whether training error reaches zero.
record.test_reason: The study motivates noisy-label detection and mitigation using prior findings on memorization. Its own results measure detection quality and clean-test accuracy, without measuring fitting of corrupted training labels or the order in which real and noisy labels are learned. Test-accuracy degradation alone does not establish V4's joint claim of perfect training fit and declining generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that FINE detects noisy labels using principal components of latent representations, with theoretical and experimental support, and improves performance across sample-selection, semi-supervised, and robust-loss applications.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains image classifiers on datasets with artificially corrupted labels and evaluates noisy-label detection and test accuracy; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard ResNet-34 clean-test accuracy decreases across 20%, 50%, and 80% symmetric noise: 87.0%, 78.2%, 53.8% on CIFAR-10 and 58.7%, 42.5%, 18.1% on CIFAR-100. Training fit is not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Validation-selected clean-test accuracy declines as symmetric label corruption increases over the tested intermediate noise levels.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports clean-test accuracy under 40% asymmetric noise, without measuring fitting of corrupted labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classification performance under structured label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: FINE's detection F-scores and downstream test accuracies evaluate label-noise detection and mitigation, rather than the extent or timing of memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Latent-representation alignment can identify noisy labels and improve robust-learning performance.

record.peer_reviewed: 35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021)
record.problems: The reported test accuracies do not establish whether training error is zero or near zero. The displayed Standard results cover only some nonzero noise fractions, not the full range from clean labels to completely random labels.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true and random labels, and convergence slowdown as corruption increases. Appendix C.5 compares filtering computation, not convergence.
Perfect fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit across corruption levels and its conjunction with steadily worsening test error from clean to completely random labels. The reported intermediate-noise test accuracies do not establish this behavior.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Real-pattern learning preceding noisy-label memorization. Detection F-score trajectories do not measure the learning order of clean and noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The cited random-label fitting and early-learning findings are prior results, not this study's evidence. No verdict is warranted for any version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether networks fit a completely random labeling to zero or near-zero training error, test at chance, and do so without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels, and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The experiments report test accuracy for some nonzero noise fractions, but do not report training error; they do not cover the full sweep from no corruption to all labels random.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, or whether they are learned differently over training.
